items.title: Smooth Gaussian polynomial data potentials

source.anchor: Original statement in runs/20261118-gaussian-potential-smooth/source-statement.txt. The pinned linked parent proves the actual joint-feature representation.
source.attribution: Original Samplinglib derivation from existing Gaussian L2 smoothness, actual potential representation and compact derivative bounds. The linked parent is not presented as an external proof of the new all-order estimate.

items.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space and let (X,Y) have joint probability law P, with X standard Gaussian and Y square integrable. For any real polynomial p and any probability rho on the unit sphere S, define the predictor and actual data potential by the integrals below. The potential V_rho is smooth on all of E. For every real radius R and derivative order n, there is a finite nonnegative constant C, chosen before rho and w, that bounds the norm of D^n V_rho(w) for every sphere probability rho and every ambient w with norm at most R.
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra. No positive dimension is assumed; an empty sphere has no probability law to instantiate.
P is a probability on E times R whose first marginal is exactly the standard Gaussian on E. The label Y is in L2(P); no independence or higher label moment is assumed.
p is any real polynomial. No parity, coefficient normalization, prescribed degree cutoff or conditional teacher relation is assumed.
For each R and n, the bound C may depend on P, p, E, R and n, but is uniform over rho and w. Order zero is included; a negative radius gives an empty spatial condition.

formulae.label: Smoothness and common local derivative bounds
formulae.tex: \begin{gathered}V_\rho\in C^\infty(E;\mathbb R)\quad(\rho\in\mathcal P(S)),\\\forall R\in\mathbb R\ \forall n\in\mathbb N\ \exists C\ge0:\\\forall\rho\in\mathcal P(S)\ \forall w\in E,\\\|w\|\le R\ \Longrightarrow\ \|D^nV_\rho(w)\|\le C.\end{gathered}

obligations.label: Derive ambient smoothness and local derivative bounds uniform over every sphere probability law

bindings.boundary: Ambient spatial regularity of the literal statistical potential only. Drift and covariance regularity, time measurability, weak-equation uniqueness, process construction, law symmetry, centering and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities require separate arguments.
